name: Brighton and Hove

licensing.selective: Selective licensing has applied since 2 September 2024 (to 1 September 2029) in four wards: Kemptown, Moulsecoomb & Bevendean, Queen's Park, and Whitehawk & Brighton Marina. A further 13 areas were approved to be phased in, with Regency and Central Hove designated from 20 October 2026, but the council says that expansion is paused while a legal challenge is reviewed: check with the council before letting there.
licensing.additional: Citywide additional HMO licensing from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2029 for HMOs of two or more storeys with three or four unrelated occupiers (single-storey flats with three or four sharers come under the selective scheme); larger HMOs need a mandatory licence.
licensing.fee: £740 for a standard selective licence (£518 on application, £222 on approval), £590–£665 with discounts, £840 if late (council fees page).

housing: Brighton and Hove has one of the largest private rented sectors outside London, with about a third of households renting privately in 2021. Much of the stock is Regency and Victorian houses converted into flats, alongside small terraces in Hanover and North Laine. Two universities create a large student market, concentrated around Moulsecoomb, Bevendean and the Lewes Road, with many shared houses. Selective and additional licensing schemes cover large parts of the city, so landlords should check a property's licence status.
checkinTips: Regency and Victorian conversions near the seafront: photograph sash windows, cornices, damp patches and any salt staining on window frames and railings.
Student HMOs around Moulsecoomb, Bevendean and the Lewes Road: photograph each bedroom door lock, fire doors, smoke alarms and the shared kitchen in detail.
Flats in converted houses: photograph the meter cupboards, communal hallway and stairs, and record keys for the street door and the flat.
Basement and lower-ground flats in Hove and Kemptown: photograph walls near floor level and light wells for damp and mould.
Steep Hanover terraces: photograph rear yards, steps and drains, and any cracks in garden walls.
Licensed properties: photograph the displayed licence or note its number, and check the room count matches the licence.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe homes to Brighton & Hove City Council's private sector housing team, which enforces housing standards and the licensing schemes.
